zh.summary: 用獨立可信來源確認特定要求及授權，搭配多層反釣魚防護並守住證據界線。

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-06｜獨立驗證與反釣魚控制
Module 09：Social Engineering（社交工程） 路線原名：Independent Verification & Anti-Phishing Controls。建議閱讀 10～15 分鐘。
一、先說結論：不要讓可疑要求，自己提供「它是真的」的唯一證明
有人傳訊息說：「我是主管，請把資料傳到這個新網址。不放心就打下面這支電話確認。」你真的打了電話，對方也說沒問題。這樣算查證完成嗎？
不一定。因為要求、電話和回答，可能都由同一個人安排。
今天要學的不是把每個人都當成騙子，而是：重要行動之前，從原本就可信的來源，確認「誰提出、究竟要做什麼、是否獲得授權」；再用多層控制，讓單一失誤不至於直接造成重大損害。
上一課 M09-05 提醒我們，合法帳號不代表每項行為都合法。本課把這個判斷變成可以執行的流程，也收束整個社交工程章節。
二、圖1：先把「要求」與「證明」放在不同的信任範圍

visual.caption: 圖 1｜信任來源與執行邊界
visual.description: 可疑訊息與獨立可信來源分開；需核對身分、特定要求與授權後才執行。

items.title: 讀圖重點
items.body: 可疑訊息與獨立可信來源分開；需核對身分、特定要求與授權後才執行。

sourceBody.text: Independent Verification（獨立驗證）：查證所使用的依據，不完全依賴正在被懷疑的訊息或對方提供的管道。
像是收到「銀行帳號異常」訊息，你不必點它的連結，而是自行開啟原本安裝、已確認的官方 App，或使用自己先前確認過的官方聯絡方式查詢。FTC 也建議使用已知真實的電話或網站，而非可疑信件提供的聯絡資訊。[FTC：辨識與避免釣魚](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-recognize-avoid-phishing-scams)
Trust Boundary（信任邊界），白話就是：這一邊的內容，還不能直接被另一邊當成可信指令。圖1把「收到的說法」與「有權執行的行動」分開；中間必須有查證與授權。
「獨立」不是只換一個 App，也不是只多問一次：

rows: 回覆原信問「真的是你嗎？」
通常沒有
原信帳號若被接管，回答仍由同一方控制
打信裡新提供的電話
通常沒有
聯絡資訊本身尚未核實
用原有通訊錄的電話回撥
有助於獨立查證
聯絡資訊不是從這封可疑訊息取得，但仍須確認具體要求
開啟既有官方系統，看核准單
有助於獨立查證
查的是既有流程中的紀錄，還要核對範圍及有效性

sourceBody.text: 獨立不是絕對安全保證。 如果原通訊錄已遭竄改，或另一個管道也被控制，仍可能失敗。所以高風險工作需要適當的核准、權限與紀錄，而不是把回撥電話當成萬靈丹。
圖中的虛線框是查核區，箭頭表示通過查核後才進入執行流程，不是網路封包一定走這條路。
三、圖2：確認的是特定行動，不只是「這是不是你的帳號」

visual.caption: 圖 2｜回撥查核：換管道，也換來源
visual.description: 依既有聯絡資料回撥，查證特定要求與核准；否認或不明時停止，而不是沿可疑訊息提供的號碼查證。

items.title: 讀圖重點
items.body: 依既有聯絡資料回撥，查證特定要求與核准；否認或不明時停止，而不是沿可疑訊息提供的號碼查證。

sourceBody.text: 我們用一個虛構例子，完整走一次。
Northstar 教材中心的行政同仁小安，收到一封看似合作廠商寄來的信：「請把學員名單改傳到新資料夾，今天就要完成。」信件附上新電話與上傳連結。
第一步：先暫停不可逆或敏感的行動。 暫時不要上傳名單，也不要輸入密碼、驗證碼或安裝遠端控制軟體。暫停不等於判定對方詐騙，而是目前的依據還不夠。
第二步：從既有可信來源找聯絡管道。 小安使用原有合作紀錄中的聯絡方式，不使用這封信新提供的電話。若找不到可信管道，就交給既有負責人或支援流程確認；不是隨便搜尋一個看起來像官方的廣告就算完成。
第三步：核對具體要求。 不只問「你有寄信嗎？」而是確認：

items: 哪一份資料？為什麼需要？
要傳到哪個已核准的目的地？誰能存取？
這次變更由誰核准？是否在合作與職務範圍內？
要做的是查閱、下載、上傳，還是變更權限？

sourceBody.text: 第四步：再檢查授權。 Authentication（身分驗證）與 Authorization（授權）不是同一關。就算真的是合作廠商，也不代表他有權取得全部學員名單。確認身分，只解決部分問題。
第五步：依結果分流。 確認要求與授權都成立，才在必要範圍執行；若對方否認、資料不一致或仍不清楚，就先保留、通報，不自行猜測後放行。真的急件，應走組織既有緊急核准流程，不是免除所有檢查。
圖2的時間由上往下，箭頭是互動先後。向既有管道查詢的箭頭，刻意不回到可疑訊息提供的新電話。這正是整張圖的重點。
四、圖3：反釣魚不是一個按鈕，而是互補的防護

visual.caption: 圖 3｜不同控制，保護不同關卡
visual.description: 五組互補控制各自保護不同關卡，沒有單一控制能保證訊息內容或行動安全。

items.title: 讀圖重點
items.body: 五組互補控制各自保護不同關卡，沒有單一控制能保證訊息內容或行動安全。

sourceBody.text: Anti-Phishing Controls（反釣魚控制措施），是降低釣魚訊息到達、降低誤操作機會、限制後果，以及支援偵測與應變的一組措施。
這接回 M01-06 的 Defense in Depth（縱深防禦）：不同層處理不同問題。只靠「員工要小心」，會把整套安全壓在一個人當下有沒有看出破綻上。NCSC 建議多層防護，也強調不能期待人員辨識每一封釣魚訊息。[NCSC：組織反釣魚防護](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/guidance/phishing)

rows: 訊息進入之前
郵件網域驗證、垃圾信與惡意連結過濾
通過過濾不等於要求合法
人準備行動時
獨立查證、敏感變更核准、清楚的通報入口
真人確認不等於所有操作都有授權
登入時
抗釣魚驗證、保護帳號復原流程
登入成功不等於付款或資料轉移已核准
行動影響範圍
最小權限、必要資料、適當複核
權限縮小不代表風險歸零
異常發生後
通報、日誌、撤銷遭濫用的存取
沒告警不代表從未發生攻擊

sourceBody.text: 圖3是「控制位置圖」，不是每次釣魚都照順序發生的固定攻擊階段。某封信可能完全不要求登入，只要求你用自己的合法帳號做錯事。
4.1 郵件上的三個英文縮寫，分別查什麼？
先把 Domain（網域）理解成網路名稱，例如教學用的 `northstar.example`。寄件顯示名稱寫「資訊部」，只是畫面文字，不是身分證明。

items: SPF（Sender Policy Framework，寄件者政策框架）：讓接收端檢查寄信來源主機，是否獲得相關寄件網域授權。它檢查的是郵件傳送層的身分，不直接保證你看到的 From 欄就是主管本人。
DKIM（DomainKeys Identified Mail，網域金鑰識別郵件）：透過數位簽章，讓接收端檢查某個簽章網域及受簽署內容的完整性。不是把信件加密，也不是替內容的誠實性背書。

DMARC（Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance，網域式郵件驗證、回報與一致性機制）：把通過的 SPF 或 DKIM 身分，與可見 From 的網域做 Alignment（對齊）檢查，並提供失敗處理政策與回報機制。不是只要任意一個網域 SPF 通過就算 DMARC 通過。 [NCSC：郵件防冒充](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/email-security-and-anti-spoofing)、[IETF RFC 9989：DMARC](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989.html)

sourceBody.text: 對齊可依規則採嚴格或寬鬆方式；這堂先掌握「檢查的網域關係必須對得上」，不要求背 DNS 設定。
若攻擊者用自己控制的相似網域寄信，他也可能把自己的驗證設定好；若真正信箱被接管，信件也可能通過驗證。因此，DMARC pass 不是「內容安全」或「主管已核准」的證書。
同樣地，HTTPS（加密的網頁連線）保護與目前網站之間的傳輸，不表示這個網站就是你原本想找的組織。釣魚網站也可能有有效憑證。不要只看鎖頭或頁面商標。
4.2 為什麼「有 MFA」還不夠？
MFA（Multi-Factor Authentication，多因素驗證）用不同種類的證明降低帳號被冒用的風險。但密碼加上手動輸入的 OTP（One-Time Password，一次性密碼），仍可能被假登入頁即時轉交給真正服務。

Phishing-Resistant Authentication（抗釣魚身分驗證）的重點，是用協定將驗證與正確服務綁定，而不是只期待使用者看出假網站。WebAuthn（網頁驗證標準）搭配適當的 FIDO2（快速線上身分驗證規格）驗證器，是這類方法的例子。相似假網域不能直接拿真網站的驗證材料來完成同一驗證。[NIST SP 800-63B-4，3.2.5](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)
這不是「裝了就不可能被騙」。它主要保護身分驗證；不會自動阻止使用者在已登入的真網站上，依假主管指示把資料交出去。帳號復原、端點安全、登入後工作階段及業務核准，仍需保護。回到圖3：每一層有自己的工作，也有自己的邊界。
五、圖4：看到一個成功訊號，別把結論放大

visual.caption: 圖 4｜看到什麼，才能推論什麼？
visual.description: DMARC通過、MFA登入成功與沒有告警各自都有有限的證明範圍；後續查證補足內容、授權與涵蓋率。

items.title: 讀圖重點
items.body: DMARC通過、MFA登入成功與沒有告警各自都有有限的證明範圍；後續查證補足內容、授權與涵蓋率。

sourceBody.text: 用證據推理時，先問「這個控制究竟證明了什麼？」

rows: 可信接收系統記錄 DMARC pass
該信符合相應網域驗證與對齊條件
信件內容真實、無惡意、要求已核准
登入系統記錄 MFA 成功
系統接受了這次驗證
每一項後續操作都是本人意願且有權執行
原有聯絡窗口否認新要求
該要求與這次獨立查證結果不一致
已確定是誰發動攻擊或用哪種技術
系統沒有告警
目前未觀測到告警；須另查產生、收集與傳遞
沒有釣魚、沒有外洩、沒有漏報

sourceBody.text: 讀郵件驗證結果，也要知道它由誰產生；不是看到信件內文自稱「已通過安全驗證」就相信。圖4逐組列出觀察與補查問題，用紅色「不等於」標出過度推論，提醒你證據有範圍。
六、如果已經點了、填了，下一步怎麼辦？
不要因為不好意思而拖延，也不要為了確認再點一次。先記下實際做到哪一步：只有開網頁、輸入帳密、提供驗證碼、下載執行檔案，還是已傳出資料？不同情況需要不同處置，點擊本身不能直接當成已遭入侵的證明。
透過既有可信管道通報；保留原訊息、時間與必要來源，避免改動證據。若驗證材料可能外洩，使用可信入口依流程更改密碼、檢查復原資訊，並由適當管理者處理有效登入狀態與異常存取。只改密碼，不應直接假設所有既有登入狀態已撤銷。
若曾執行不明程式或傳出敏感資料，交由有權人員依事件應變流程處理。不要自行轉寄可疑附件給全體同事，也不要查閱無關個人資料。這是把 M01-07 的事件應變，接到本章實際情境。
我們這次只用虛構情境推理，不對第三方寄測試釣魚信，也不收集任何真實密碼或驗證碼。
七、看圖推理：三個小檢核

items: 1. 對方傳來新電話，你照著回撥，對方確認要求。圖1中哪條信任關係還沒建立？你會改用什麼依據？
2. 一封信 DMARC 通過，登入又使用抗釣魚驗證，為什麼仍不能直接把名單上傳到信裡的新位置？請指出圖3還需要哪一類控制。
3. 小安已輸入密碼，但尚未確認有異常登入。現在能確認什麼、不能確認什麼？你會先採取哪兩項行動，而不是等待損害出現？

sourceBody.text: 參考解答另備供網站預設收合區；公布答案不代表你已作答或學會。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：1. 原訊息提供的新電話，為什麼不算充分獨立驗證？
paragraphs: 要求與查證電話可能同屬對方控制，因此「對方再次確認」沒有補上可信來源到特定要求的連結。改用既有、先前核實的聯絡紀錄或正式系統，確認具體資料、目的地、用途與核准。換 App 或多問一次本身不夠；可信管道也要適當維護。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：2. DMARC 通過且抗釣魚登入，為什麼仍不能直接上傳？
paragraphs: DMARC 檢查網域驗證與對齊，抗釣魚驗證保護登入，兩者都不替資料移轉的用途與目的地核准。仍須獨立核實這項要求，確認分享權限、核准對象、最少資料與必要複核。真的帳號也可能被濫用，真的使用者也可能被誘導做錯事。

sourceBody.summary: 參考解答：3. 已輸入密碼但尚無異常登入證據，怎麼判讀與處置？
paragraphs: 能確認的是曾提供密碼，驗證材料可能暴露；尚不能宣稱已成功接管或已外洩資料。先透過可信入口依流程更改可能暴露的密碼並通報，保留原訊息與時間。由適當管理者核查登入、復原設定及有效工作階段，必要時撤銷存取；不等待損害才保護帳號，也不假設改密碼已處理所有登入狀態。

sourceBody.text: 八、把本章收成一句話
信任不能取代驗證；驗證不能取代授權；任何單一控制，也不能取代整體防護。
M09-01～05 教你辨識不同信任濫用；M09-06 把查證、技術防護與證據界線接成可執行流程。下一個路線單元 M02-01 會進入被動與主動偵察：同樣要問資料從哪裡來、能支持什麼判斷，以及哪些活動需要授權。

en.summary: Verify specific requests and authorization through independent trusted sources, with layered anti-phishing controls and bounded evidence.

sourceBody.text: CEH M09-06 | Independent Verification & Anti-Phishing Controls
Module 09: Social Engineering. Suggested reading: 10–15 minutes.
1. The main idea: a suspicious request must not supply its only proof of authenticity
Someone sends: “I am your manager. Upload the records to this new website. If you are unsure, call the number below.” You call, and the person confirms. Have you verified the request?
Not necessarily. The request, telephone number, and answer may all be controlled by the same person.

The goal is not to distrust everyone. Before a sensitive action, use an already trusted source to confirm who is asking, exactly what is requested, and whether it is authorized. Complement that process with multiple controls so a single mistake does not immediately cause major harm.
M09-05 distinguished legitimate accounts from legitimate actions. This unit turns that distinction into a usable workflow and brings the social-engineering chapter together.
2. Figure 1: separate the request from its evidence

visual.caption: 1 | Trust sources and action boundaries
visual.description: Separate an untrusted request from a known source. Verify identity, specific request and authority before acting.

items.title: How to read the diagram
items.body: Separate an untrusted request from a known source. Verify identity, specific request and authority before acting.

sourceBody.text: Independent verification uses evidence that does not depend entirely on the message or channel being questioned.

For a message claiming a bank-account problem, open the previously verified official app or use established contact details rather than following the message. The FTC recommends a phone number or website known to be genuine, not the details provided by a suspicious message. [FTC guidance](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-recognize-avoid-phishing-scams)

A trust boundary separates information that has not yet been accepted as trustworthy from the authority to take action. Figure 1 puts the claim on one side and the protected action on the other; verification and authorization sit between them.
Changing apps or asking twice does not by itself create independent evidence.

rows: Reply to the original email: “Is this really you?”
Usually not
Whoever controls a compromised account may also answer
Call the new number in that email
Usually not
The contact details are themselves unverified
Call a number in an established directory
Helps
Its source is independent of this message; still verify the specific request
Check an approval in the established business system
Helps
Check its scope and validity, not just its existence

sourceBody.text: Independence is not an absolute guarantee. An established directory may have been altered, or another channel may also be compromised. High-risk work still needs suitable approvals, permissions, and records. A callback is not a universal solution.
The dashed boundary in Figure 1 encloses verification; the arrow leads to action only after verification. It is not a required network-packet path.
3. Figure 2: verify a specific action, not just an account

visual.caption: 2 | Callback: change channel AND source
visual.description: Call a number from an established source. Verify the specific request and approval. Stop when denied or unclear.

items.title: How to read the diagram
items.body: Call a number from an established source. Verify the specific request and approval. Stop when denied or unclear.

sourceBody.text: Consider a fictional organization, Northstar Learning Centre. An administrator receives an apparent vendor email: “Upload the learner list to a replacement folder today.” It includes a new phone number and upload link.

First, pause sensitive or difficult-to-reverse actions. Do not upload the list, enter passwords or codes, or install remote-control software. Pausing does not accuse the sender of fraud; the evidence is currently insufficient.

Second, find an established trusted channel. Use contact information from existing vendor records, not the new number. If there is no trustworthy channel, ask the established owner or support process to verify. An apparently official search advertisement is not automatically a reliable substitute.
Third, confirm the details. “Did you send an email?” is too broad. Ask:

items: Which records are needed, and for what purpose?
Which approved destination will receive them, and who can access it?
Who approved the change? Is it within the relationship and role?
Is the requested operation viewing, downloading, uploading, or changing permissions?

sourceBody.text: Fourth, check authorization. Authentication and authorization are different gates. Even a genuine vendor may not be entitled to the complete learner list. Establishing identity resolves only part of the problem.

Fifth, branch on the result. Execute only the necessary scope when the request and authority are established. A denial, discrepancy, or unresolved question means hold and report rather than guess and proceed. Urgent work should use an established emergency-approval process, not an exemption from every check.
Time runs downward in Figure 2; arrows show interactions. The verification arrow intentionally goes to established contact details, not back to the number supplied by the suspicious message.
4. Figure 3: anti-phishing is a set of complementary controls

visual.caption: 3 | Different controls, different gates
visual.description: Five complementary control areas protect different gates. No single check proves message or action safety.

items.title: How to read the diagram
items.body: Five complementary control areas protect different gates. No single check proves message or action safety.

sourceBody.text: Anti-phishing controls reduce malicious messages reaching users, reduce unsafe actions, limit consequences, and support detection and response.

This connects to M01-06 defense in depth. Different layers address different problems. “Employees must be careful” places too much reliance on a person spotting every deception at the right moment. The NCSC recommends a layered approach rather than expecting staff to identify every phishing message. [NCSC guidance](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/guidance/phishing)

headers: What it cannot establish by itself
rows: Before message delivery
Domain authentication, spam and malicious-link filtering
A delivered message is not necessarily a legitimate request
Before a person acts
Independent checks, sensitive-change approval, easy reporting
A real person's confirmation is not blanket authorization
At sign-in
Phishing-resistant authentication; protected account recovery
Successful sign-in does not approve a transaction
Around the impact
Least privilege, necessary data only, appropriate second review
Limited permissions do not eliminate risk
After unusual activity
Reporting, logs, revocation of abused access
No alert does not establish no attack

sourceBody.text: Figure 3 maps control locations; it is not a fixed attack sequence. Some phishing asks for no login at all: it persuades someone to misuse access they already possess.
4.1 What do SPF, DKIM, and DMARC check?
A domain is an Internet name, such as the teaching example `northstar.example`. A sender display name saying “IT Department” is screen text, not identity proof.

items: Sender Policy Framework (SPF) checks whether the sending host is authorized for the relevant transmission-level sender domain. It does not directly establish that the visible From field identifies your manager.
DomainKeys Identified Mail (DKIM) uses a digital signature to verify a signing domain and the integrity of signed content. It does not encrypt the message or certify the honesty of its claims.

Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance (DMARC) checks alignment between the visible From domain and a passing SPF or DKIM identity, and provides policy/reporting mechanisms. SPF passing for just any domain is insufficient. [NCSC email anti-spoofing](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/email-security-and-anti-spoofing), [IETF RFC 9989](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9989.html)

sourceBody.text: Alignment can be strict or relaxed under the relevant rules. For now, understand the required relationship between domains rather than memorizing DNS configuration.

An attacker-controlled lookalike domain may authenticate its own email successfully. A compromised genuine mailbox may also send authenticated email. Consequently, DMARC pass is not a certificate of safe content or managerial approval.

Likewise, HTTPS protects transport to the website being visited; it does not prove that the site is the organization you intended to reach. Phishing sites may have valid certificates. A padlock or logo is not sufficient.
4.2 Why is “we have MFA” insufficient?

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) uses different categories of evidence to reduce account impersonation. However, a password and a manually entered one-time password (OTP) can still be relayed from a counterfeit login page to the genuine service.

Phishing-resistant authentication binds authentication to the correct service through the protocol, rather than relying only on user vigilance. Web Authentication (WebAuthn), used with appropriate FIDO2 authenticators, is an example. A lookalike domain cannot simply reuse the genuine site's authentication material to complete that authentication. [NIST SP 800-63B-4, section 3.2.5](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html#phishres)

That does not mean the user cannot be deceived. Authentication protection does not automatically stop a signed-in user following a fake manager's instruction to share records. Recovery, endpoint security, post-login sessions, and business approvals still need protection. Each layer has a purpose and a boundary.

sourceBody.text: Ask what a control actually establishes.

rows: A trusted receiving system records DMARC pass
Relevant authentication and alignment requirements were met
Honest content, harmless links, or approved action
The sign-in system records successful MFA
The system accepted authentication evidence
Every subsequent operation reflects the account holder's intent and authority
An established contact denies the new request
The request conflicts with this independent check
The attacker's identity or exact technique
No system alert
No alert observed; generation, collection, and delivery still need checking
No phishing, no disclosure, or no missed detection

sourceBody.text: Know who produced an authentication result. “Security verified” written in a message body is not a trusted system result. Figure 4 groups observations with follow-up checks and uses red “not equal” labels to identify unsupported leaps.
6. What if you already clicked or entered information?

Do not delay out of embarrassment or click again to investigate. Record what actually happened: opening a page, entering a password, entering a code, executing a download, or sending records. Different actions require different responses. A click alone does not prove compromise.

Report through an established trusted channel. Preserve the original message, time, and necessary source information without altering evidence. If authentication material may be exposed, use a trusted entry point to follow the password and recovery-information process, and have appropriate administrators address active sessions and unusual access. A password change should not be assumed to revoke every existing session.

If unknown software ran or sensitive records were sent, authorized responders should follow the incident process. Do not forward suspicious attachments to everyone or inspect unrelated private information. This applies M01-07 incident response to social engineering.
This lesson uses fictional reasoning only. It does not send phishing tests to third parties or collect real passwords or authentication codes.
7. Reason from the diagrams: three short checks

items: 1. You call the new number supplied in a message and receive confirmation. Which trust relationship is still missing in Figure 1? What source would you use instead?

2. An email passes DMARC and your login uses phishing-resistant authentication. Why can you not immediately upload the learner list to its new destination? Identify the missing category of control in Figure 3.
3. An administrator entered a password, but unusual sign-in has not been confirmed. What is known and unknown? Name two immediate actions rather than waiting for visible damage.

sourceBody.text: Reference answers are prepared separately for the website's closed-by-default answer section. Publishing answers is not evidence that the learner answered or understood.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: 1. Why is the new number insufficiently independent?
paragraphs: The request and telephone number may be controlled by the same party. Reconfirmation does not establish a trusted connection to the particular request. Use previously verified records or the established system to verify data, destination, purpose, and approval. Switching apps or asking twice is insufficient; trusted channels also need maintenance.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: 2. Why do DMARC and phishing-resistant sign-in not authorize the upload?
paragraphs: DMARC checks domain authentication and alignment; phishing-resistant authentication protects sign-in. Neither approves the purpose or destination of a data transfer. Independently verify the request, sharing authority, approved recipients, minimum data, and required review. A genuine account can be abused, and a genuine user can be manipulated.

sourceBody.summary: Reference answer: 3. What is known and what should happen after password entry?
paragraphs: Password entry is known and authentication material may be exposed. Successful takeover or data disclosure is not yet established. Use a trusted entry point to follow the password-change process, report, and preserve the message and time. Appropriate administrators should review sign-ins, recovery settings, and active sessions and revoke access as needed. Do not wait for visible damage or assume a password change handled every session.

sourceBody.text: 8. The chapter in one sentence
Trust does not replace verification; verification does not replace authorization; one control does not replace the whole defense.

M09-01 through M09-05 introduced forms of trust abuse. M09-06 connects verification, technical controls, and evidence boundaries into a practical workflow. The next route unit, M02-01, covers passive and active reconnaissance: again ask where information comes from, what it supports, and what requires authorization.
